text_excerpts.1:
Procedures to Obtain Permits for Barricading, 
Excavating and/or Construction in Public Right-of-way 
 
 
As required by City Ordinance, anyone working within City right-of-way is required to 
obtain a permit. The documents below must be on file in our system prior to submitting 
an application: 
 
1. Contractor must present evidence of at least $2,000,000 in general liability 
insurance coverage, by providing the original of a Certificate of Insurance, 
which shows the certificate holder as follows: 
City of Albuquerque 
Department of Municipal Development 
Construction Coordination Section 
PO BOX 1293 
Albuquerque, NM, 87103 
2. To perform excavation work, Contractor must have and provide a copy of a State 
License GF-09, GF-98, MM-98, EL-01, or EE-98. 
3. To perform concrete work, contractor must have and provide a copy of a State 
License GA-01, GA-02, GA-03, or GA-98. 
4. If excavating any part of the right-of-way, contractor must post and provide the 
original of a $10,000 Contractor’s Excavation Bond using the City’s approved 
form. 
5. If performing concrete work, must post and provide the original of an additional 
$5,000 Contractor’s Sidewalk, Curb, and Gutter Bond using the City’s 
approved form. 
6. If performing a water tap, must provide a water tapping bond associated with the 
activity in question. 
 
 
All documents may be emailed to dmdccs@cabq.gov, or sent to our office.

saved_evidence.basis: This is an earlier version of the Contractor's Excavation Bond, not a duplicate of the current one. Three measured differences, all substantive: the penal sum is FIVE THOUSAND DOLLARS ($5,000) where the current form reads TEN THOUSAND DOLLARS ($10,000); it cites the "Street Excavation Ordinance, 6-5-2-3 (A)(3), (R.O. 1994)" where the current form cites the "Street Excavation & Barricading Ordinance, 6-5-2-3 (A)(2), (R.O. 2005)"; and its header reads "Revised 05/04/01" against the current form's 5-1-05 footer.
saved_evidence.measurement: Against the current form src-aeb5714315a45302: normalized-text similarity only 0.4426 despite token coverage 0.9709 / 0.9382. High token overlap with low sequence similarity is exactly the signature of a re-versioned boilerplate instrument, and it is why a hash-only or a token-only check would both have mis-called this pair.
saved_evidence.currency_note: Both versions are live on the City page at the same time with no version label in either filename, so a contractor downloading ContractorExcavationBond.pdf today gets the superseded 2001 instrument. That is a City publication problem, not an inventory problem, but it is the reason this record must not be published as the current bond form.
